To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MDD patients are less sensitive to the SSRI paroxetine-induced inhibition on the growth of PBMDs compared to healthy volunteers, and that the reduced sensitivity is associated with a lower expression of the SERT co-factor ITGB3 in the PBMC.
PBMC growth inhibition by paroxetine is significantly reduced in patients with MDD, and that the expression of ITGB3 is lower in PBMCs of patients with MDD compared with healthy volunteers.
PBMCs growth is sensitive to antidepressant drugs in vitro and that the sensitivity to paroxetine is decreased in depressed patients compared with healthy controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel MDD biomarker based on the ex vivo growth-inhibition of PBMCs by paroxetine.
the identification of a novel biomarker for MDD, which can help to prioritize TR patients for alternative treatments.
the identification of novel antidepressant drug biomarkers for the prioritization of TR MDD patients for alternative therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PBMC paroxetine sensitivity test may be a potential biomarker for MDD and TR MDD patients and that the ITGB3 expression may be a potential mechanism underlying the reduced paroxetine sensitivity in MDD patients.
PBMC sensitivity to paroxetine is decreased in patients with MDD compared with healthy controls and that this difference is reduced by antidepressants in TS but not in TR patients.
the lower paroxetine sensitivity in PBMCs of TR-MDD patients is a trait marker, whereas in MDD patients it is a state marker.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lower sensitivity of PBMCs to paroxetine in MDD patients is a state marker of the disorder and may be useful for identifying TR MDD patients.
MDD patients have a decreased sensitivity to the growth inhibitory effects of paroxetine on PBMCs compared with healthy controls and this is reversed by antidepressant treatment.
MDD patients have decreased sensitivity to SSRI-induced inhibition on PBMCs growth, which may reflect a state marker of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low paroxetine sensitivity phenotype of PBMCs is observed in patients with MDD, and that this phenotype is reversed by antidepressant drug treatment.
PBMCs paroxetiene sensitivity may be used for the identification of MDD patients who are at risk of treatment resistance.
the reduced sensitivity to SSRI-induced inhibition is associated with TR MDD and may be a useful biomarker to identify MDD patients that will not respond to SSRI treatment.
